flashcards.q: Where must ACL filtering be enforced in a production RAG system?
flashcards.a: At the database/ANN retrieval layer as a mandatory predicate on every query -- never as a post-retrieval application-layer discard step. A missed filter is a data breach, not a bug.

flashcards.q: Are Pinecone namespaces a cryptographic isolation boundary?
flashcards.a: No -- Pinecone documents namespaces as a logical, query-time partition. Scales cheaply to 100,000+ tenants but a misconfigured query can still cross it. Weaviate's per-tenant HNSW shards give stronger physical isolation instead.

flashcards.q: Why must PII be handled at ingestion rather than at generation/output time?
flashcards.a: Once sensitive text is embedded into a vector and indexed, you cannot un-embed it -- it will be retrieved whenever a query is semantically close. Output-time filtering can't prevent the PII from having already been retrieved and placed in the model's context.

flashcards.q: What breaks if you add new documents with a new embedding model without re-embedding the existing corpus?
flashcards.a: Vectors from different embedding models don't share a geometry -- similarity between them is meaningless. Symptom: silent, gradual, uneven retrieval quality decline, not a loud failure.

flashcards.q: Describe the blue-green zero-downtime index migration pattern.
flashcards.a: Build the new index fully in parallel while the old one serves traffic; dual-write during the build window; validate against a golden query set; atomically swap an alias; retain the old index (~24h) for rollback.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't HNSW support clean deletes, and what's the operational consequence?
flashcards.a: Removing a node requires re-linking its neighbors, expensive to do online, so deleted vectors are tombstoned instead. Tombstone accumulation degrades search quality/latency over time, requiring periodic compaction or rebuild.

flashcards.q: Where does the cost in a typical production RAG query actually go?
flashcards.a: Query embedding and vector search are cheap (ms, tiny fraction of cost); reranking is moderate; generation (context + question + answer tokens) dominates. Optimize generation model choice and retrieval precision first, not vector search infra.

flashcards.q: What's the risk of a nightly batch sync between a source permission system and RAG index ACL metadata?
flashcards.a: A staleness window exists between a permission revocation and it taking effect in retrieval -- up to the sync interval length -- during which a revoked user can still retrieve documents. Fix: webhook-driven, near-real-time ACL updates.

flashcards.q: Why did production systems move from RBAC to ABAC for retrieval filtering?
flashcards.a: RBAC (coarse roles/tenant membership) is too coarse for real enterprise permissions. ABAC filters on finer attributes (department, classification, owner) that map to how access is actually granted -- at the cost of more filter-aware query complexity.

flashcards.q: Why is Postgres row-level security valuable as defense-in-depth beyond application-layer filtering?
flashcards.a: RLS is enforced by the database regardless of query shape -- a query that forgets the tenant_id WHERE clause still can't see other tenants' rows, because Postgres blocks it structurally rather than relying on every code path remembering the filter.
